title: Move NanoBanana Pro to OpenRouter
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Routes `nanobanana-pro` through OpenRouter’s pinned Google AI Studio endpoint with fallback disabled.
- Preserves 1K/2K/4K selection, default reasoning, 14 references, pricing, EXIF, and content-policy 400 responses.
- Direct 4K generation (5504×3072, 49.0s), 2K editing (2400×1792, 22.3s), and local E2E (21.2s) passed with exact billing and cache.
- Focused stack verification after syncing `main`: 26/26 Gen image/access tests and 287/287 Enter aliases/pricing tests.
- Accepted product differences: OpenRouter combines text/image prompt tokens, and its image catalog exposes no safety-settings passthrough. Total billing remains exact; OpenRouter’s own content policy still applies.

gist.headline: NanoBanana takes the scenic route
gist.blurb: NanoBanana Pro now travels through OpenRouter's pinned Google AI Studio path. The pixels, resolutions, references, billing, and sensible refusal behavior all made the trip intact.
gist.summary: Routed the `nanobanana-pro` image model through OpenRouter's pinned Google AI Studio endpoint with fallback disabled, while preserving 1K/2K/4K generation, 14 reference images, default reasoning, EXIF, exact billing, and content-policy 400 responses.
gist.impact: Users can keep using NanoBanana Pro for direct 4K generation and 2K editing with the same resolution choices, pricing, caching, and reference-image capacity through the new provider route.
gist.visual_concept: Depict NanoBanana Pro as a cozy pixel-art banana-shaped image parcel traveling along a well-marked garden path from a retro terminal to an OpenRouter signpost, with clear 1K, 2K, and 4K seed packets beside it. Polli, wearing a tiny courier cap, carefully guides the parcel while a CRT monitor robot checks a bill and a row of 14 little reference-picture frames grows like flowers; this represents the provider move while the model's capabilities and accounting remain intact.
